taxonomy.subtopic: Diffuse alveolar damage and hyaline membranes

questions.stem_html:
A 46-year-old man is admitted with septic shock from an obstructed urinary tract. Two days later, he develops severe hypoxemia, bilateral air-space opacities, and a PaO2/FIO2 ratio of 92 despite positive-pressure ventilation. Echocardiography shows normal left ventricular systolic function. A pressure-volume curve demonstrates markedly reduced lung compliance. An illustrated lung section shows eosinophilic material lining collapsed alveoli.

Which primary pathophysiologic change produced these findings?

options.text_html: Selective constriction of pulmonary veins with preserved barrier integrity
Surfactant overproduction that increases alveolar surface tension
Diffuse injury to alveolar epithelium and capillary endothelium with protein-rich leakage
Left ventricular failure causing a purely hydrostatic transudate
Bronchiolar smooth-muscle spasm causing uneven ventilation

questions.explanation_html: Inflammatory injury disrupts both sides of the alveolar-capillary barrier. Protein-rich edema, fibrin, and necrotic epithelial debris form hyaline membranes; surfactant dysfunction and collapse reduce compliance. ARDS is a noncardiogenic permeability edema caused by diffuse alveolar-capillary injury, classically producing hyaline membranes and severe shunt physiology.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: Pulmonary venoconstriction alone would raise hydrostatic pressure but would not cause diffuse alveolar damage and hyaline membranes.
wrong_choice_explanations.2: Surfactant deficiency or inactivation, not excess production, contributes to alveolar collapse in ARDS.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Normal cardiac function and protein-rich permeability edema argue against cardiogenic pulmonary edema.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Bronchospasm causes airflow obstruction, not diffuse bilateral permeability edema with low compliance.

questions.educational_objective: Identify diffuse alveolar damage as the morphologic substrate of ARDS and connect barrier disruption to protein-rich edema, hyaline membranes, low compliance, and refractory hypoxemia.
